headline: A US federal judge has thrown out antitrust lawsuits by Penske Media and Chegg that accused Google of using their content for its AI Overviews.
score_reason: Ruling was on 30 Sep 2026, before the edition window; lowered one point.
importance_line: Publishers who say AI search summaries take their readers lose a main legal argument, though the ruling covers antitrust claims only and the compensation question is unresolved.
summary: WinBuzzer reports that Judge Amit Mehta ruled on 30 Sep 2026 that Penske Media and Chegg had not shown the agreement their reciprocal-dealing claims need, writing "an expectation is not an agreement", and that their claim that Google forced AI Overviews on search users failed because he treated them as one product. The ruling covers only these antitrust claims and does not decide whether Google may use copyrighted material, and ColombiaOne notes reports differ on whether Penske may refile.
notes: Pool item came from ColombiaOne, a rewrite of other outlets; credited WinBuzzer. Score 6 to 5, stale.
